mainTopic: Whether a shutter or bolt must be tied to be used on שבת: רבי ירמיה's proof from the נגר הנגרר, רבי אבא's reply from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and רבי יוחנן's ruling
overview: The משנה earlier argued about closing a window with a shutter (פקק החלון) on שבת. רבי אליעזר permits it only if the shutter is tied and hanging, while the חכמים are more lenient. רבי אבא's tradition states the lenient view this way: the shutter may be used whether it is tied or not, as long as it was prepared for this use. רבי ירמיה objects that the lenient view still requires tying and only drops the need for hanging. He proves this from the parallel dispute about a נגר הנגרר (a dragging door-bolt). The proof draws on three sources: a ruling of רבי יוחנן, a משנה, a ברייתא, and עולא's identification of the strict opinion as רבי אליעזר. רבי אבא answers that his wording follows a ברייתא in which רבן שמעון בן גמליאל permits a prepared bolt even if it is untied. רבי יוחנן rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. The גמרא then begins to challenge that ruling from a משנה about vessel covers, and the challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The lenient view: tied or not, as long as it is prepared
steps.stepSummary: A ruling (begun on the previous amud) sums up the lenient view on the shutter: it may be used whether tied or untied, as long as it was prepared for this purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whether it is tied or not tied, it is permitted, as long as it was prepared for this use.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a ruling that started on the previous amud. It says the shutter may be used whether or not it is tied, as long as it was set up ahead of time to be a shutter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this version, being tied is not required at all. The only condition is preparation (מתוקן), meaning the item was designated and fitted as a shutter. This is the claim רבי ירמיה will challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Tied or attached (to the door or window)
That it is prepared or fitted for this purpose
'And that is', meaning 'provided that'. It introduces a condition.

phrases.english: Both if it is tied and if it is not tied,
provided that it is prepared.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּין קָשׁוּר בֵּין שֶׁאֵינוֹ קָשׁוּר, וְהוּא שֶׁמְּתוּקָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a statement begun earlier (attributed there to רבי אבא's tradition)
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under the lenient view, a shutter is permitted whether tied or not, as long as it was prepared for use as a shutter.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה proposes a stricter wording
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה challenges the wording. He says the lenient view should be: hanging or not hanging, but it must be tied.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said to him: Let the Master say instead: whether it is hanging or not hanging, as long as it is tied!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה objects to the ruling. He says the lenient opinion still requires the shutter to be tied, and only drops the need for it to be hanging.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two versions disagree about an untied shutter. In step 1 an untied shutter is fine if it was prepared. רבי ירמיה says an untied shutter is never fine, and the only thing the חכמים forgive is that it need not hang. He backs this up with the proof in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And let the Master say'. A polite way of proposing a different formulation.
Hanging (suspended from the door or window)

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two conditions apart. 'Tied' (קשור) means attached at all. 'Hanging' (תלוי) means dangling from that attachment. רבי ירמיה requires the first but not the second.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said to him,
And let the Master say:
Both if it is hanging and if it is not hanging,
provided that it is tied!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה, וְלֵימָא מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the formulation given in step 1 and offers a replacement
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that under the lenient view an untied (but prepared) shutter is permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The lenient opinion still requires tying. It is only lenient about hanging, so an untied shutter should be forbidden.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן links the shutter dispute to the dragging bolt
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה starts his proof. רבי יוחנן said the shutter dispute is the same as the dispute about a נגר הנגרר.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Just like the dispute here, so is the dispute about a dragging bolt.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first step of רבי ירמיה's proof. רבי יוחנן says the shutter argument and the dragging-bolt argument follow the same lines. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא will quote the bolt source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the two disputes match, whatever the bolt sources reveal about the lenient opinion also applies to the shutter. רבי ירמיה will use the definitions given for the bolt to learn what the חכמים require for the shutter.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'dragging bolt'. A locking pole attached to the door that drags along the ground.
Like the dispute here

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: As Rabba bar bar Chana said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Like the dispute here,
so is the dispute about a dragging bolt.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the proof for רבי ירמיה's wording
steps.raayaObject: רבי ירמיה's claim that the lenient view requires tying
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's statement that the shutter dispute mirrors the dragging-bolt dispute

steps.title: The משנה about the dragging bolt
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a dragging bolt may be used in the מקדש but not elsewhere, and a loose bolt is forbidden in both places. רבי יהודה is more lenient in each case.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: A dragging bolt, one may lock with it in the Temple but not in the country. A bolt that is just placed is forbidden in both places. רבי יהודה says: The placed bolt is permitted in the Temple, and the dragging bolt is permitted in the country.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה that רבי יוחנן was referring to. It lays out two opinions about locking a door with a bolt on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion allows the dragging bolt only in the מקדש, because rabbinic decrees do not apply there. A loose (מונח) bolt is forbidden everywhere. רבי יהודה shifts each case one level more lenient: the loose bolt is allowed in the מקדש, and the dragging bolt is allowed even outside it.

keyTerms.meaning: One locks (a door)
The Temple
The 'country', meaning anywhere outside the Temple
The one that is simply placed, not attached to the door

phrases.english: As we learned: A dragging bolt,
one may lock with it in the Temple,
but not in the country.
And the placed one, here and there, is forbidden.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
The placed one is permitted in the Temple,
and the dragging one is permitted in the country.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: נֶגֶר הַנִּגְרָר, נוֹעֲלִין בּוֹ בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the משנה that רבי יוחנן's comparison refers to
steps.raayaObject: Identifying which positions match in the two disputes
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about the dragging bolt (מסכת עירובין)

steps.title: The ברייתא defines the dragging bolt
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא defines the dragging bolt as tied, hanging, and touching the ground. רבי יהודה permits that even outside the מקדש and forbids only a bolt that is neither tied nor hanging.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: What is the dragging bolt that one may lock with in the Temple but not in the country? Any bolt that is tied and hanging, with its end reaching the ground. רבי יהודה says: This one is permitted even in the country. Rather, which one is forbidden in the country? Any bolt that is neither tied nor hanging, which one removes and puts in a corner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains exactly what each opinion means by 'dragging bolt'. This gives רבי ירמיה the details he needs for his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the forbidden case is a bolt that is 'neither tied nor hanging'. That implies a bolt that is tied but not hanging is permitted. So the lenient opinion still requires tying and only drops the hanging requirement, which matches רבי ירמיה's wording.

keyTerms.meaning: Its end reaches the ground
He removes it (detaches it)
A corner

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the double negative 'לא קשור ולא תלוי' (neither tied nor hanging). Only a bolt missing both is forbidden for רבי יהודה. This is the key detail of the proof.

phrases.english: And it was taught: What is a dragging bolt

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנּוֹעֲלִין בּוֹ בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ אֲבָל לֹא בִּמְדִינָה?
phrases.english: that one locks with in the Temple but not in the country?
Any that is tied and hanging
and its end reaches the ground.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
This one is permitted even in the country.
Rather, which is forbidden in the country?

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ לֹא קָשׁוּר וְלָא תָּלוּי,
phrases.english: Any that is neither tied nor hanging,
and one removes it and places it in a corner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the cases mentioned in the משנה of step 4
steps.raayaObject: רבי ירמיה's claim that the lenient opinion requires tying but not hanging
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's definition: רבי יהודה forbids only a bolt that is neither tied nor hanging

steps.title: עולא identifies the first opinion as רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: עולא says the first opinion about the dragging bolt is רבי אליעזר. This links it to רבי אליעזר's strict view in the shutter משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע בר אבא said in the name of עולא: Who taught the law of the dragging bolt? It is רבי אליעזר!
steps.whatsHappening: עולא names the author of the strict first opinion: it is רבי אליעזר. This places each side of the bolt dispute next to its side in the shutter dispute, and it completes רבי ירמיה's proof. The next step gives רבי אבא's reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the strict first opinion is רבי אליעזר, then רבי יהודה's lenient view lines up with the חכמים of the shutter משנה. The חכמים would then require tying but not hanging, just as רבי ירמיה said.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of
Who is the תנא (author) of this teaching?

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ירמיה's proof works like a chain. Shutter dispute = bolt dispute (רבי יוחנן). The strict opinion = רבי אליעזר (עולא). The lenient opinion forbids only 'neither tied nor hanging' (the ברייתא). Therefore the חכמים require 'tied' but not 'hanging'.
steps.whyThisMatters: Identifying the author of an anonymous opinion is what allows the גמרא to move a rule from one dispute to the other.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בַּר אַבָּא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּעוּלָּא:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua bar Abba said in the name of Ulla:
Who is the Tanna of the dragging bolt?
It is Rabbi Eliezer!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בַּר אַבָּא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּעוּלָּא: מַאן תַּנָּא נֶגֶר הַנִּגְרָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the author of the first opinion, connecting the bolt sources to the shutter dispute
steps.raayaObject: Matching each opinion in the bolt dispute to its counterpart in the shutter dispute
steps.raayaSupportSource: עולא's identification of the first opinion as רבי אליעזר

steps.title: רבי אבא says his view follows a known תנא
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא answers רבי ירמיה. He says he holds like a specific תנא, and he is about to quote that תנא's ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I am the one who says it this way, like this תנא, as it was taught in a ברייתא:
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא answers רבי ירמיה's challenge by saying his own wording has a source. This line sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ירמיה argued that the lenient view must still require the bolt to be tied. רבי אבא does not back down. He says there is a תנא who does not require tying at all, so his wording is justified.

keyTerms.meaning: I am the one who says it this way
Like this תנא (an earlier sage of the משנה period)

phrases.english: He said to him: I am the one who says it
phrases.notes: רבי אבא is answering רבי ירמיה.

phrases.english: like this tanna, as it was taught:
phrases.notes: Sets up the ברייתא quoted in the next step.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא דַּאֲמַרִי כִּי הַאי תַּנָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי ירמיה's challenge and his proof built from the dragging bolt dispute.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Source attribution: the disputed wording matches an existing tannaitic opinion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No known opinion would allow a bolt that is not tied, so רבי אבא's wording seemed wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is a תנא (רבן שמעון בן גמליאל) who allows it if it was prepared, even untied.

steps.title: The ברייתא about a reed set up as a door bolt
steps.stepSummary: The ת"ק allows the reed only if it is tied and hanging at the doorway. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows it if it was prepared for this use, even if it is not tied.
steps.simpleTranslation: A reed that the homeowner set up to open and lock the door with: when it is tied and hanging at the doorway, one may open and lock with it. If it is not tied and hanging, one may not open and lock with it. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: if it was prepared for this, it is allowed even though it is not tied.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the ברייתא that רבי אבא uses as his support. It shows a תנא who does not require the bolt to be tied.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ת"ק needs a physical connection to the door, meaning tied and hanging. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that preparing the reed for this job is enough, even without tying it. That lenient view is exactly what רבי אבא needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A reed or stick
That the homeowner set up or prepared
Opens and locks
Tied and hanging
Prepared or designated for the purpose

steps.whyThisMatters: It introduces the idea that designating an object for use as a bolt can stand in for physically attaching it. This opens the way for רבי יוחנן's ruling in the next step.

phrases.english: A reed that the homeowner set up
to open and lock the door with it,
when it is tied and hanging at the doorway —
one may open and lock with it,
if it is not tied and hanging —
one may not open and lock with it.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: מְתוּקָּן, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ קָשׁוּר.
phrases.english: If it was prepared, it is allowed even though it is not tied.
phrases.notes: This is the lenient view רבי אבא relies on.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָנֶה שֶׁהִתְקִינוֹ בַּעַל הַבַּיִת לִהְיוֹת פּוֹתֵחַ וְנוֹעֵל בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the actual text of the תנא that רבי אבא mentioned.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אבא's wording that the lenient view does not require tying.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא (תוספתא) with the opinion of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: Through a chain of transmitters, רבי יוחנן rules that the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, so a prepared bolt is allowed even if it is not tied.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה בר שילת said in the name of רב אסי, who said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a practical ruling on the ברייתא: we follow the lenient view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling turns רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's lenient view into the accepted הלכה. A reed prepared as a bolt may be used on שבת even if it is not tied. This ruling is about to be challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, a bolt that was prepared for its job may be used on שבת even if it is not tied.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda bar Sheilat said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: that Rav Asi said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The halacha follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בַּר שִׁילַת אָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling on the dispute in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: a prepared bolt is allowed even if it is not tied.

steps.title: Did רבי יוחנן really say this? Challenge from vessel covers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יוחנן really ruled this way and begins to quote a משנה about vessel covers that seems to contradict him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי יוחנן really say this? But we learned in a משנה: All covers of vessels...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a challenge against רבי יוחנן's ruling. It starts quoting a משנה, and the quote continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The formula "ומי אמר רבי יוחנן הכי" signals that a contradiction is coming between this ruling and another position of רבי יוחנן. The משנה about vessel covers is the base text for that contradiction. Its details and the problem it raises appear on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Did he really say this? (opens a contradiction)
Covers of vessels

steps.confusionAlert: The quote stops in the middle. The actual contradiction has not been stated yet, so don't try to work it out from this line alone.

phrases.english: Did Rabbi Yochanan really say this?
But didn't we learn: All covers of vessels
phrases.notes: The quote continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָכִי? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling just attributed to רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה about vessel covers (which will be completed next) seems to clash with this ruling of רבי יוחנן.
